policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: The variant adds only the article with γυναῖκες. ASV 'In like manner, ye wives' renders a vocative address either way; English marks no Greek article here.
ASV 'that, even if any obey not the word' renders the ascensive καί with 'even'; the omitting reading leaves no source for that word.
ASV 'a meek and quiet spirit' keeps meek before quiet, which excludes the transposed r01; r00-base and r02 differ only in the orthography of πραέως/πρᾳέος and are indistinguishable in English.
ASV 'who hoped in God' renders εἰς and ἐπί with θεόν alike; the English preposition 'in' does not distinguish them.
Aorist ὑπήκουσεν and imperfect ὑπήκουεν are both carried by ASV's simple past 'as Sarah obeyed Abraham'; nothing in the English marks the aspect.

ASV 'as being also joint-heirs of the grace of life' supplies 'being' and leaves the case unmarked; neither the dative agreeing with the wives nor the nominative agreeing with the husbands is excluded by the English.
ASV ends the list with 'humbleminded', which renders ταπεινόφρονες; φιλόφρονες would give 'courteous'.
ASV moves straight from 'contrariwise blessing' to 'for hereunto were ye called' with no participle of knowing; the added εἰδότες goes unrendered.
ASV 'Let him refrain his tongue from evil' supplies the possessive that English idiom requires for the Greek article; it does not attest an explicit αὐτοῦ.
ASV 'And his lips that they speak no guile' uses the same idiomatic possessive for the articular χείλη; the English cannot show whether αὐτοῦ stood in the text.
ASV begins the line 'And let him turn away from evil', rendering the connective δέ that the omitting reading lacks.
ASV 'if ye be zealous of that which is good' renders ζηλωταί; μιμηταί would give 'followers/imitators'.
ASV 'sanctify in your hearts Christ as Lord' names Christ as the object, rendering Χριστόν rather than θεόν.
ASV joins 'being ready always to give answer' with a colon and no connective, but an unrendered δέ is ordinary English practice; the absence does not exclude the longer reading.

The clause ἀλλὰ μετὰ πραΰτητος καὶ φόβου that opens SBLGNT 3:16 is rendered by ASV's adversative 'yet with meekness and fear', printed at the end of its verse 15; the omitting reading leaves 'yet' without a source.
ASV 'wherein ye are spoken against' is passive with no object clause; the longer reading καταλαλοῦσιν ὑμῶν ὡς κακοποιῶν would require 'they speak against you as evil-doers'.

ASV reads 'Christ also suffered for sins once' and relegates the alternative to the mapped textual note 'Many ancient authorities read died', so the text renders ἔπαθεν and ἀπέθανεν is the noted variant.
ASV 'that he might bring us to God' renders the first-person ἡμᾶς, not ὑμᾶς.
ὀλίγοι and ὀλίγαι differ only in gender; ASV 'wherein few, that is, eight souls, were saved' shows no gender on 'few'.
ASV 'doth now save you' has the second person, which requires ὑμᾶς; the RP reading reads ἡμᾶς ('us') and also reorders the phrase.
The variant adds only the article before θεοῦ; ASV 'on the right hand of God' renders either, since English marks no article on the proper reference.
